newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 10.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Ireland - June 10.

text.p: The following are the highlights of stories from the Irish press on Tuesday.
- Fianna Fail and Progressive Democrat negotiating teams will have their first meeting in Dublin this afternoon and expect to have agreed a programme for government by the weekend.

- EU leaders will be involved in a frenetic series of meetings, starting today, to see whether a key element of the single currency plan can be ratified at next Monday's Amsterdam summit. - The price of new houses rose by an average of over 14 percent to 73,523 punts in the year to end March.

- Fianna Fail leader Bertie Ahern is still facing an anxious wait before he knows the exact strength of his Dail (parliament) power base as a recount for the final seat in the Dublin southeast constituency resumes today.
- The new French socialist government rocked plans for monetary union yesterday by refusing to sign up to a hard-won pact which sets out economic rules for running the single currency.
- A number of Christian Brothers and former brothers are to face sex abuse charges arising out of incidents at a boys' industrial school.
- Negotiations between Fianna Fail and the Progressive Democrats on a programme for government, which begin in earnest this afternoon, are expected to be completed by Friday.
- In a first warning on the economy for Bertie Ahern, European finance ministers have advised a tough line on public spending to cut Ireland's budget deficit.
- Confirmation that the body, found in the Shannon Estuary at the weekend, was not Jo Jo Dullard's, got a mixed reaction from the missing Kilkenny girl's family.
